messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Results with tip ranges shifted to the left by one.
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] Results with tip ranges shifted to the left by one.
messages.body_plain:
This is probably due to having include_null_range=TRUE in the ML inference, but having include_null_range=FALSE in the plotting?  (The null range is always the first range in the ranges_list, if present).

I ran the example script right now and it came out fine, so it may be that you changed something or have an old script.

Also -- make sure you're using the current version of BioGeoBEARS on GitHub, not an old version.

If none of that helps, please send me all scripts and input files.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Confused by BAYAREALIKE+J-similar input trees but different results
messages.subject_clean: Confused by BAYAREALIKE+J-similar input trees but different results
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nick and group members:

Hi! I am trying to run an BAYAREALIKE+J analysis.  I've followed your most recent example script and modify it to my own data. The pipeline works well but when I changed the input tree with a new one with slightly changed branch lengths, the result changed dramatically.

I also tested the dataset with RASP under the same BAYAREALIKE+J model (best fitted),  but resulting in nearly indentical distribution of estimated ancestral range.  I have no idea what has happened.

I have attached my script and input files. hope these files be helpful for you to find out the problem.

I am looking forward to any advice.
THANKS!
Best wishes

QJ Zhou

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Confused by BAYAREALIKE+J-similar input trees but different results
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] Confused by BAYAREALIKE+J-similar input trees but different results
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

It's hard to tell with just this information and without the output graphics, but those two trees are "flipped" with respect to each other.

If you ran the inference on one tree, but then inserted a new tree and tried to plot the results on the new tree, this would result in very messed-up results.  The probabilities-of-ancestral-states results are tied to a specific tree, flipping the tree will put the wrong probabilities on the wrong nodes.

 To fix it, re-run the inference from scratch with the new tree.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Confused by BAYAREALIKE+J-similar input trees but different results
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] Confused by BAYAREALIKE+J-similar input trees but different results
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nick,

Thanks for your kindly reply.

Actually the two trees were applied seperately to the full pipeline, from tree file input to model select. The difference between results located only in a small but important part of ~10 nodes, around the center of backbone of  the trees, and shouldn't result from flipped tree topology. These nodes seemed sensitive to small changes of input.

The results files are attached. you can easily find the difference.

Many thanks.

QJ Zhou
